about: I have a history of consulting for diverse social sector organizations. about:
I’m a management consultant at Deloitte focused on helping clients transform how they operate, build, and deliver by enabling next-gen business operations. My work spans operational strategy, MES and PLM enablement, software-defined transformation, and large-scale program delivery — with a core focus on execution, not just vision.

I’ve supported clients in industries including aerospace & defense, semiconductors, medtech, autonomous vehicles, and manufacturing/industrial goods, driving digital transformation across complex value chains and high-stakes environments. I bring experience designing future-state operating models by facilitating cross-functional workshops, conducting stakeholder interviews, and using value stream mapping to uncover improvement opportunities — all while building transformation roadmaps that align business and technology stakeholders.

My international education through the World Bachelor in Business program — at USC, HKUST, and Bocconi — shaped my ability to lead in diverse, global teams and adapt to complexity and change. 

I’m especially passionate about bridging strategy with execution and helping organizations stay competitive through smarter, software-driven operations. I’m always open to conversations around operational excellence, emerging tech, and opportunities where innovation meets execution

volunteering.description:
As a member of the Associate Board, I sought to raise awareness of the CFB, fundraise to support the CFB's mission, volunteer around the warehouse, and assist on strategic initiatives, such as the annual report and website.

The mission of the Chicago Furniture Bank is to provide dignity, stability, and comfort to Chicagoans that face poverty by allowing clients to handpick an entire home's worth of furniture. 

The Chicago Furniture Bank is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization, founded in July of 2018, that serves as an intermediary between Chicagoans who have extra furniture and those who need it. We provide furnishing packages to our clients that include beds, couches, armchairs, dressers, desks, end tables, coffee tables, kitchen tables + chairs, dish ware, rugs, lamps, artwork, mirrors, and more.

During my high school years I often volunteered weekday nights at Feed My Starving Children in Schaumburg, IL. I helped to package easy to make meals consisting of all essential nutrients that would then be shipped globally, both as disaster relief food and food for impoverished communities. I still volunteer while I am back home on break from school.

projects.title: Multi Modal Image Captioning
projects.description:
This project evaluates different approaches to building an AI system that can automatically generate natural-language descriptions of images (image captioning). It's particularly aimed at researchers and developers working on accessibility technology, as image captioning can help make visual content accessible to visually impaired users. This study specifically compares:

- Different AI model configurations and optimization strategies
- Various techniques for converting images and text into formats the AI can understand
- Different training approaches on both local computers and cloud systems

projects.title: ReasonForge: Modular mathematics toolkit for LLMs
projects.description:
ReasonForge is a mathematics toolkit that integrates with Claude and other LLMs via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Instead of letting LLMs guess at calculations, it routes mathematical operations through SymPy, NumPy, and SciPy returning provably correct results.

The problem: LLMs produce plausible-looking but incorrect answers on math problems 15-30% of the time. For research, finance, or engineering applications, "usually right" isn't good enough.

The solution: 111 tools across 7 domain-specific servers covering logic, algebra, calculus, statistics, geometry, and physics. The LLM handles natural language understanding; ReasonForge handles the actual math.

Key features:
- Modular architecture - install only what you need (85-90% context token reduction vs. monolithic approach)
- Production-ready symbolic reasoning package with 13 tools
- Built on proven libraries: SymPy, NumPy, SciPy

projects.title: TransitGuard - Safety predictions for Chicago public transit
projects.description:
TransitGuard is a predictive safety platform for the Chicago Transit Authority (CTA), built as my capstone project for Northwestern University's MS in Data Science.

The problem: The CTA serves 950,000+ daily riders, but safety incident reporting is reactive — passengers and authorities only learn about problems after they happen.

The solution: We analyzed 50,000+ CTA-related crime incidents (2014-2024) alongside ridership patterns, streetlight outages, and environmental factors to identify high-risk stations, routes, and time windows before incidents occur.

Key findings:
- CTA trains have 3x more incidents than buses despite lower ridership
- Theft and battery account for 52% of all CTA-related crimes
- DBSCAN spatial clustering identified persistent hotspots across the rail network

What I built:
- Predictive models (XGBoost, Logistic Regression, time series forecasting)
- RAG-powered chatbot using FastAPI, Pinecone, and Claude for natural language safety queries
- Mobile app with real-time alerts (React Native)

Built with a 5-person team. My contributions: GenAI development, mobile app development, and predictive modeling.

headline: Digital Government Solutions | Public Sector Consulting | Board Governance
about:
My career spans around 30 years of experience in Information Technology, Consulting, Cyber Security and Project Management for both the private and public sectors. Currently, I am serving as a Principal Technical Project Manager for the Commonwealth of Kentucky for more than two decades and involved in transforming the Business into a Technology solution.

My prior expertise includes, international exposure with blue chip clients in a wide variety of organizations in having held executive positions in countries like India, Singapore and Malaysia. 

I have been focusing on establishing an ecosystem of cross-functional technology solutions and engaged in enterprise-wide business transformation consulting for private and public sectors including the state and local government along with core expertise focused on customer centricity.

Additionally, I have represented wide variety of organizations and chapters and involved in putting together numerous events and presented at several conferences across the United States and globally. My efforts have been well recognized with several awards and honors and holds professional membership and affiliations in various associations.

I am a Frankfort, Kentucky resident and have remained active with my alma mater and most recently, I was  appointed to a six-year term until 2022 on to the Eastern Kentucky University (EKU) Board of Regents by Kentucky Governor.

My passion to give back, propelled me to be active on numerous boards, including currently serving as a President for the PMI Bluegrass Chapter, Lexington, Kentucky and has served as a Vice President of Strategic Planning in the past. PMI serves the needs of the Project Management community.

In addition to my Certified Kentucky Paralegal (CKP) credential and Project Management Professional (PMP) credential, and Information Systems Audit (CISA) credential and Cyber Security Credential (CISM) and  Certified Data Privacy Solutions Engineer (CDPSE), I hold a Bachelor's in Electronics and Communication Engineering and an MBA from Eastern Kentucky University.

During my spare time, I connect with and offer assistance to numerous communities, and also enjoy running and doing workouts. Last but not the least, I love travelling and I have visited five continents and twenty two countries in the world.

headline: Strategy Advisor to C-Suites & Boards | Former Fortune 200 C-Suite Executive | Author & University Educator | Guides High-Performing Leaders
about:
I serve CEOs, boards, and senior executive teams as a strategy advisor and thinking partner—work informed by decades as a Fortune 200 C-suite executive, strategy consultant, and educator at Kellogg and Harvard University. 

My background spans enterprise strategy, business-model reinvention, sustainability, and large-scale performance improvement. Earlier in my career, I created Walmart’s first enterprise strategic planning process and ran it for 3 years (600%+ market value increase). As EVP and Chief Knowledge Officer at a $15B retailer/wholesaler, I co-founded and operated a limited-assortment store chain, managed a $3B supply alliance, and led major transformations in IT, marketing, and operations. I have also advised senior leaders at Apple, McDonald’s, AT&T, IBM, and other global companies navigating strategic inflection points.

At Deloitte, I serve as a senior leader in our Strategy practice, focusing on creating shareholder value through sustainability levers. I work alongside executive teams to shape innovation strategies, long-term value plans, organizational resilience, and enterprise transformations. My client work includes innovation strategy for the USPS and sustainability strategy for the International Olympic Committee. I have also held global leadership roles, including leading Deloitte’s client response to COVID-19 and in programs supporting our largest multinational clients.

A core part of my work centers on leadership performance. I design and deliver executive development experiences—including Deloitte’s Marquee Manager Experience, where 145 alumni have advanced to partner or managing director. I co-led the “Deep Purpose: The Next Way to Win” program at Harvard for C-level executives and previously served eight years on the Kellogg School of Management faculty.
My current focus integrates two parallel lifecycles:- the 𝗼𝗿𝗴𝗮𝗻𝗶𝘇𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗹𝗶𝗳𝗲𝗰𝘆𝗰𝗹𝗲 (strategy, growth, operations, finance, change), and- the 𝗲𝘅𝗲𝗰𝘂𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗱𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹𝗼𝗽𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗹𝗶𝗳𝗲𝗰𝘆𝗰𝗹𝗲 (identity, maturity, purpose, decision-making). Aligning these lifecycles creates clarity, accelerates transformation, and improves enterprise performance.

I am the author of 𝑊𝑎𝑙-𝑆𝑚𝑎𝑟𝑡 (McGraw-Hill), host of Deloitte’s 𝐵𝑒𝑐𝑜𝑚𝑖𝑛𝑔 𝑅𝑒𝑠𝑖𝑙𝑖𝑒𝑛𝑡 podcast, and have appeared as a thought leader in the Wall Street Journal, CNN, CNBC, and other outlets. My academic background in philosophy and ongoing study toward certification as a spiritual director inform the reflective, grounded approach I bring to senior leaders navigating complexity.

publications.title: Cracking prediction of asphalt concrete using fracture and strength tests
publications.publishedAt: International Journal of Pavement Engineering · Mar 11, 2021
publications.description: Strength and fracture-based tests have been developed to assess the cracking potential of asphalt concrete (AC). The major difference between them is the presence of a notch in fracture tests. The objective of this study was to investigate the correlations between AC strengths and energy-based indices obtained from these tests, theoretically and experimentally. Theoretically, the role of a notch is presented and validated experimentally using 13 various AC mixtures. Strength tests, Indirect Tensile Test (IDT) and Indirect Tensile Cracking Test (IDEAL-CT), and a fracture test, Illinois Flexibility Index Test (I-FIT) were used. In addition, digital image correlation (DIC) was utilised to monitor crack development and path, compute crack propagation speed, and identify location and mode of energy dissipation. Brittle AC exhibits limited plasticity in both strength and fracture tests. Hence, a correlation is, theoretically, expected between strength and fracture test results. Conversely, ductile AC exhibits high plasticity in a strength test, but limited plasticity in a fracture test due to the notch presence, which amplifies the stress around the crack tip. Hence, theoretically, no correlation is expected between strength and fracture test results. Both tests reported lower index values for brittle AC mixtures, but no trend for ductile AC mixtures. Using DIC, the process zone (PZ) magnitudes of strength specimens, such as IDEAL-CT, were greater than the fracture-process zone (FPZ) for fracture specimens, such as I-FIT. Although I-FIT exhibits a single well-defined crack path, its Flexibility Index (FI) variability is a direct result of crack propagation speed, which is a function of the AC inhomogeneity. The FI captures AC material-inherent variability, which is useful for AC risk assessment to control AC pavement premature cracking.

about:
Susannah has 15 years of consulting experience in corporate environmental strategies, and is currently a Senior Manager in Sustainability Strategy & Transformation in Deloitte Consulting's Strategy practice. Her latest client work involves shaping industry and CEO agendas on ESG topics including climate change and sustainable products and services. 

Susannah is the Sustainability leader for the Deloitte US Chemicals Practice and Deputy lead for US Energy & Chemicals Industry Sustainability. Previously, she lead the Deloitte US Integrated Climate services team, structuring end-to-end support for clients on their Path to Net Zero.

Her consulting teams design data-driven models and tools to guide sectors, industries, and companies toward a lower emissions future. She is also scaling circular economy, plastics, and packaging sustainability work for the US firm, and has driven ground-breaking work in sustainable sourcing, packaging and plastic waste mitigation, and materials end-of-life management for companies in the energy, retail, and consumer products industries. 

As a Yale graduate student, Susannah completed a number of consulting projects for food and beverage, telecommunications, and healthcare companies. Engagements included a global supply chain risk analysis, agricultural GHG emissions reduction strategy, customer lifetime value calculation, and corporate water management program. Before graduate school, Susannah managed a five-person team at Eastern Research Group, Inc., developing and implementing federal environmental partnership programs for U.S. EPA. 

Susannah has an MBA from the Yale School of Management, Masters in Environmental Management (MEM) from the Yale School of Forestry and Environmental Studies, and a BA in American History and Environmental Policy from Northwestern University. She is also a devoted alumni mentor for the Environmental Defense Fund (EDF) Climate Corps program for graduate students studying business and the environment.

I currently serve as the Chicago Office Tax Managing Partner (OTMP), responsible for leading our tax professionals in this market. In this role, I work with our teams and other leaders to understand our clients’ needs and help them achieve their tax planning and business goals.  In addition, I am committed to developing the next generation of leaders with deep technical skills and broad industry experiences to bring relevant insights to their clients.

I previously served as Deloitte Private’s US Family Enterprise leader, helping multi-generational businesses navigate the considerations associated with family-owned enterprises. For the past 25 years, it has been my passion and purpose to strategically advise private companies and their owners throughout their business lifecycle, including generational transitions.  

My broad range of experience includes income, gift and estate tax planning for privately owned businesses, single-family offices, and their owners. I advise privately owned businesses on topics ranging from acquisitions and incentive compensation to entity structuring and effective federal and state income tax planning. I also advise family offices on topics including standing up newly created family offices and family investment partnerships, process and technology transformation, and enterprise risk management. My broad range of client experiences has equipped me with the deep knowledge needed to help clients identify and address their issues and opportunities, including assessing capital needs, preparing the next generation of owners to be active board members, and establishing philanthropic and community relations strategies. 

All this work is supported by the talented professionals throughout the organization who deliver a suite of holistic capabilities, including audit & assurance, consulting, tax, and risk and financial advisory services.

Thoughts and views expressed are my own.

experience.description:
Aleye is a revolutionary community for women living with PCOS that puts the management of her health and body back in her hands.
PCOS is the leading endocrine disorder that affects up to 1 in 5 of those designated female at birth. BUT symptoms of PCOS are highly individualized and present themselves in different ways and women today do not receive adequate care to support their health holistically. 

We are building a lifestyle recommendation and management system to help women identify the best long term changes to make for their individual symptoms and capabilities, access detailed and easily understandable information to actually execute on these recommendations, and hold themselves accountable using evidence-based methods to create sustainable habits.
Technology Consultant with experience in technology strategy, advising and implementation of Salesforce in the Healthcare and Financial Services space.

publications.description: If we are to think about the post-SDGs agenda, it would be worth considering using a new approach to set new goals and targets. One new approach could be an opportunity seeking approach. This approach is a change from the current problem-solving approach, which is more proactive and focused on exploring new vectors to realize new goals. Using this approach, one potential goal that could be considered for the post-SDGs agenda is an adaption of Artificial Intelligence. However, scarce financial and human (experts) capitals could be obstacles to install artificial intelligence systems into developing countries. To fill these gaps, promotion of space satellites to run and support artificial intelligence systems will be indispensable.

publications.title: How to reduce US space expenses through competitive and cooperative approaches
publications.description:
Space policy analysis of major space countries: US, Russia, China,  ESA, and Japan. 
One of the difficulty that space policy makers has is to identify sound reasons to justify enormous expense of space activities to compete among other national priorities. Risk and funding sharing is one way to reduce overall space expense. To achieve this, international cooperation is key. Thus, this paper addressed how and what area of space activities could be cooperated among space-faring nations.

headline: I-O Psychologist | Organizational Development Manager | Training and Development Lead
about:
Ever since I was a young adult, sitting in my Industrial/Organizational (I/O) Psychology class on campus, I knew from that moment I wanted…no, needed to be an I/O Psychologist. Here I am, 10 years later obtaining my doctorate. It is with a diverse background of experience in human resources, mental healthcare, leadership, administrative support, and military intelligence, that my passion is now deep rooted.

Here are a few things about me that I think you should know: 
1)	I thoroughly enjoy any type of research or learning opportunities. 
2)	I educate and drive myself to be a better overall person for myself, my family, my community and the company I work for.
3)	I love to analyze and solve organizational problems with modern solutions that make sense. 
4)	If you want to get something done the right way - come to me (Known Fact).

I have a strong work ethic and I love to showcase my abilities in areas including workforce analytics, psychometrics, diversity and inclusion, developing formal training plans/materials, career coaching, and measuring organizational effectiveness. I/O Psychology has unlocked so many opportunities in my career and I continue to find new ways to grow. 

Professional Skills
Microsoft Word | Microsoft Office| Statistical Data Analysis | Organizational Evaluation | Survey Programming | Workforce Equity | Diversity and Inclusion | Training and Development | Organizational Effectiveness | Career Coaching | Workforce Analytics | Change Management | Maintaining Employee Satisfaction | Professional Resume Writing | Research and Analysis | Labor Relations

I enjoy meeting new people and hearing perspectives on various topics in the I/O Psych world. Feel free to reach out if you wish to talk about experiences and new ideas in I/O Psychology.

publications.title: Prevention Strategies of Emergency Management and Disaster Professionals Battling Burnout
publications.description: Burnout in the world of public services, particularly in emergency and disaster management, can be a paradox. Two standard modes of operations often exist, including steady state (blue sky) operations of prevention and planning activities amid conflicting priorities and politizing events and the activation (grey sky) operations of responding to incidents, disasters, and crises. These two high-stress modes of operation, coupled with added pressure from leadership and resource limitations, increase undue stress in a first responder environment without the protections and resources afforded most first responders. This chapter will review and discuss the background and causal impacts of burnout in emergency and disaster management, provide recommendations and strategies for prevention and recovery and evidence-based practices, and leave you with additional considerations for your jurisdiction, policies, and/or practices.

publications.title: THE CAPABLE EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT PROFESSIONAL: EMERGING COMPETENCIES FOR A CHANGING WORLD
publications.description: The increasingly complex risks associated with emergent issues in emergency management, compounded with problems existing in organizational structures, are beginning to outpace the institutional ability to address them, leading to more significant losses and damages in several communities. The responsibilities of emergency management agencies continue to expand, and many may need more resources and knowledge to address them. This chapter will survey the literature to highlight what will be discussed as the critical competencies of the everyday emergency manager from an international paradigm. We approach this by across governance structures. In our discussion, we cover various topics ranging from current higher education programs, certifications (by state, country, and international), and the gaps identified by emergency managers internationally. The ability of emergency management professionals to adequately meet a standard level of performance has far-reaching implications for community resilience, engagement, and trust. It can also close the performance gap by applying leadership, management, critical thinking, and decision-making strategies.

publications.title: A Climate Change Paradigm and Its Effects on Emergency Operations Center Decision-Making Process
publications.description: The correlation between climate change and its impacts on hurricane risk has also impacted the decision-making process of emergency managers, Emergency Operations Centers (EOCs), and elected officials at every level of government. This correlation between meteorologists, for example, and multi-jurisdictional cooperation at all levels of government drives decision-making for all within the context of hurricane risk. This paradigm has been reflected in case studies and training to enhance the capability of professionals using emergency decision-making processes with ever-developing disasters while maintaining working capability under mental distress. The findings in this chapter are intended to identify hurricane risk through the lens of climate change and introduce its impacts on emergency management professionals and managers operating in the ever-evolving disaster management space. This understanding of the complexities of disaster and emergency decision-making not only has to improve for the practitioner continuously but also be translatable and understood by the elected officials who grant delegation of authority (DOA), that provide resources and personnel and finally impacts the ability and capability of Emergency Management Departments (EMDs) and organizations within their jurisdiction. Improving the decision-making process and supporting the whole community and its stakeholders promotes safety, reduces loss of life, and enhances EOC operations at various levels.

publications.title: Burnout and Retention
publications.description: In emergency management (EM), the landscape of incoming professionals is evolving from second-career professionals to first-career college graduated practitioners. This change spotlights the difference between management and leadership and its effects on the retention and burnout of professionals. EM professionals see growth in organizations, with “projected growth between 2016 and 2026 to be around 8%” states Columbia Southern University. Issues and gaps inside the EM field or ecosystem become even more apparent when the severity of and damages related to an incident or event increase.

about:
I’m a public relations leader who blends creativity and strategy, shaping stories with precision and purpose to build reputation and influence. At Deloitte, I counsel managing partners and senior leaders across key markets on communications, media relations, and digital best practices.

My career began in PR agencies focused on technology, where I learned to make the complex clear. That foundation still shapes my approach today: blending analytical rigor with creative storytelling to position leaders as trusted voices.

Born and raised in Verona, Italy, I carry my heritage into everything I do. A proud Boston College alumna, I embrace the Ignatian ideal of setting the world aflame through purpose-driven work.

During my 13+ years in PR—including eight at Deloitte—I’ve guided executives through pivotal industry moments, from Tax Reform to the Tech IPO boom, elevating them across diverse markets.

Outside of work, you’ll usually find me on the Peloton leaderboard, buried in a book, or mapping out my next trip. Since relocating from New York City to the Bay Area in 2019, I live with my husband, daughter, and two cats—the best audience I’ll ever have.

experience.description: As a Public Relations Manager on Deloitte’s U.S. Markets Team, I support the San Francisco, Los Angeles, Denver and Seattle markets—four priority geographies within the West region—as well as the Chicago market. I advise each market’s Managing Partner and senior leaders on media relations, executive visibility, and social media strategy. I also lead the development and execution of tailored PR campaigns that strengthen Deloitte’s brand, amplify leadership voices, and support local business growth.

headline: Cyber Risk Leader ★ Helping organizations fortify their cyber security posture
about:
Accomplished cyber leader with over 16 years of consulting experience. Has successfully delivered on projects for Fortune 100 clients by integrating cyber security and compliance activities throughout the ERP transformation lifecycle. Strong communicator with the ability to build consensus and influence without authority across various organizational levels on the value of cyber risk. Possess considerable knowledge of business processes and operations through exposure of ERP environments. Extensive experience operating in global team environments spanning multiple continents, time zones, and languages. Deep technical acumen and a passion for continuous learning via professional and personal (“homelab”) experiences.

Leo’s experience spans the following key areas:
► CYBER DOMAIN EXPERTISE: Application assessment and architecture, role-based access control (RBAC), privileged access management (PAM), identity and access management (IAM), application controls, security testing, secure deployment, and cyber strategy & governance.
► PROJECT MANAGEMENT AND EXECUTION: Has led globally distributed project teams of up to 20 members in delivery of professional consulting services, including project shaping, planning, scoping, budgets, timelines, risks, and issues.
► PRACTICE DEVELOPMENT: Contributed to knowledge capital, researched emerging services, enhanced consulting methodologies, developed custom tools using Java and MS Access.
► TALENT DEVELOPMENT: Responsible for developing talent, including development and delivery of training to global audiences (400+ members), coaching & mentoring of staff, and recruiting (both campus and experienced hire channels).
► BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT: Attained $7M+ USD in sales on an annual basis, co-led client sales pursuits, participated in eminence building activities, authored and delivered client proposals, built trusted business advisor relationships, and developed statement of work (SOW) documents.

projects.title: The Role of AI & Machine Learning in Identity Governance
projects.description: This research paper examines how AI-powered identity governance is becoming essential for cybersecurity and risk management in today’s expanding digital environments. As organizations increasingly rely on cloud services, remote work, and third-party tools, traditional IAM systems struggle to scale and enforce policies in real time. These gaps expose organizations to unauthorized access, insider threats, and compliance failures. By leveraging AI and machine learning, identity governance solutions can deliver real-time monitoring, behavioral analytics, and automated access control—dynamically adjusting permissions based on risk context and user behavior. This paper presents real-world use cases showing how AI-driven identity governance improves security, reduces privilege misuse, and enhances operational efficiency across sectors.

projects.title: IDENTITY THREAT DETECTION AND RESPONSE (ITDR): THE NEXT BIG THING IN CYBERSECURITY
projects.description: This research paper explores the growing importance of Identity Threat Detection and Response (ITDR) in combating identity-based cyberattacks. As traditional tools like firewalls and antivirus solutions fail to detect credential misuse and privilege escalation, ITDR offers a proactive approach using AI-driven analytics and real-time monitoring. By integrating with frameworks such as Zero Trust and Identity and Access Management (IAM), ITDR enhances threat visibility and automated response. The paper highlights how ITDR reduces insider threats, prevents account takeovers, and strengthens organizational resilience in an increasingly digital threat landscape.

headline: Salesforce Marketing Cloud Architecture Leader @ Deloitte | 7x Certified | ex-Salesforce
about: Robert is a 10+ year Salesforce Marketing Cloud SME, specializing in designing and developing scalable architectures with a focus on platform integration, data governance, and solution flexibility. His experience encompasses the deployment of thousands of campaigns, the design of hundreds of customer journeys, and the implementation of dozens of scalable architectures using Salesforce and Adobe platforms. Possessing a unique blend of technical expertise and a background in design and engineering, Robert excels at translating complex business requirements into actionable solutions that resonate with customer, marketing, and IT audiences.

experience.description:
Technical Leadership

• Operate as the primary Salesforce Marketing Cloud product owner, effectively translating stakeholder needs into actionable strategies and driving successful implementation of both high-level and low-level designs.
• Partner with executive stakeholders to develop Salesforce cross-cloud solutions and cross-platform integrations and architectures including Adobe, Braze, Google Cloud Platform, Amazon, and Microsoft; designed to maximize the effectiveness of each platform, architecture, and team.

receivedRecommendations.description:

Robert is a tremendously talented and experienced solutions architect specializing in marketing technology. He led our teams through: 1. formulation and conception of new multi-channel marketing journeys; 2. data discovery and journey audits; 3. automation improvements and analysis; 4. CDP segment definitions and strategies; 5. audience targeting best practices; 6. troubleshooting and support escalations; and 7. improvements to ways of working and marketing processes.

Robert is a seasoned consultant, and he brings a client service lens to every project he works on. He is always quick to recommend a more efficient or more effective process where available, and he helps clients understand how solutions will impact the customer experience. He is great at talking to highly technical resources, and also great at translating concepts so that they are easy to understand for less-technical stakeholders.

Robert is a talented manager. He understands the needs of the business, and he is great at coordinating resources and getting things done. He is an open and effective communicator, and he is patient in reserving judgment and holding on decision-making until he has all the necessary information. He is proactive in setting up his team members for success by asking great questions and anticipating what they need to succeed. He takes on a lot of responsibility and consistently delivers amazing results.

As a mentor, Robert is unmatched. He leads technology trainings and helps new team members navigate the business. He goes out of his way to make sure people are feeling informed and supported. His enthusiasm and curiosity is infectious. He is great at stepping back where appropriate and helping his team members find their own way, but he is also happy to take ownership when needed to help push a project or deliverable across the finish line. Working with Robert helped me level up my own understanding of technology, consulting, and leadership. I would recommend working with Robert in any capacity, and I would recommend following his advice.

headline: Partner - Accounting, Controls and Reporting Advisory at Deloitte
about: Lauren is a partner in Deloitte's Accounting, Controls and Reporting Advisory practice based in Chicago. Lauren's passion is assisting clients with their financial reporting and technical accounting needs throughout a company's lifecycle. In her role, Lauren advises clients on various accounting and financial reporting issues. Lauren is passionate about assisting clients navigate complex capital market transactions, including public exits via IPO or SPAC, and assisting clients on the adoption of new accounting standards.

experience.position: Partner - Accounting, Controls and Reporting Advisory
Senior Manager - Accounting and Reporting Advisory

experience.description:
Lauren specializes in supporting audit teams and developing firm technical accounting positions in the following areas, under both U.S. GAAP and IFRS:
- Current and future-state revenue recognition accounting, including application of the guidance to specific industries including software, life sciences, and automotive
- Current and future-state lease accounting
- Current-state consolidation accounting

In her role, Lauren has assisted with the development of various firm publications, including A Roadmap to Applying the New Revenue Recognition Standard (issued September 2016) and the TRG Snapshot for Revenue Recognition (issued November 2016).

Additionally, Lauren is a frequent speaker at client presentations related to the new revenue recognition and leases standards.

Prior to beginning her rotation in Deloitte's National Office Accounting Services practice, Lauren was a Deloitte Advisory manager, and provided advisory services to clients across multiple industries, including telecommunications, technology, and automotive.

Lauren primarily focused on assisting companies assess the accounting and operational impacts of the new revenue recognition standard (ASU 2014-09 / IFRS 15).  As part of the assessment process, Lauren tailored and applied knowledge obtained from working on the FASB's revenue recognition project to client-specific facts and circumstances.

Lauren is actively engaged in the firm's revenue recognition efforts, which includes preparing materials for and presenting at revenue recognition conferences.

Postgraduate Technical Assistant for the joint Revenue Recognition project.

Researched, co-authored, and presented four memorandums to the FASB and IASB board members during the redeliberations of the 2011 Exposure Draft, "Revenue from Contracts with Customers".  Memorandums included:
- Contract modifications (IASB Agenda ref 7A / FASB Agenda ref 163A)
- Contract costs (IASB Agenda ref 7B / FASB Agenda ref 165B)
- Effect of the revenue recognition model on asset managers (IASB Agenda ref 7C / FASB Agenda ref 166C)
- Disclosures: contract costs, onerous performance obligations, and qualitative information (IASB Agenda ref 7C / FASB Agenda ref 167C)

Assisted in the drafting process of the Revenue from Contracts with Customers fatal flaw document that was issued to external reviewers for comment in June 2013.

Organized, attended, and documented outreach activities held with preparers, users, auditors, and regulators to understand the implications of the Revenue Recognition standard on constituents in various industries and jurisdictions.

Taught four sections of the Introduction to Financial Accounting course, which is the first accounting course that all undergraduate business students must take upon admittance to the Tippie College of Business.

Lauren was awarded the Byron R. Ross Award for Teaching Excellence based on her performance as a teaching assistant and feedback from student evaluations.
Assisted in the audits of 3 public companies in the Chicagoland area.

about:
One of my core purposes is to inspire others to believe in themselves and show them that I genuinely care about their success. I believe that the most impactful way to achieve success is by investing in our own personal growth. My focus is on the trials and tribulations we face, many of which we allow to define who we are. I believe that when it comes to hardships within our control, it's essential to acknowledge our mistakes—not as losses, but as opportunities for growth and valuable lessons.

I am currently a Tax Consultant at Deloitte in Chicago, specializing in multi-state taxation. Prior to this role, I held two seasonal positions as a Tax Preparer. In my first position, I worked at a private accounting practice with two professors/attorneys, where I assisted with both tax-related and law-related matters. In my second role, I worked remotely for a large public accounting firm, preparing 1040 tax returns for high-net-worth individuals.

My goal for the near future is to sit for the CPA exam, and I’m excited to continue advancing in my professional journey. I look forward to the connections I’ll make along the way. Professional development is always a priority for me, and I’m actively working on building a strong network. If you'd like to connect or know of any opportunities that align with my skill set, feel free to reach out to me here on LinkedIn!

"The best investment by far is anything that develops yourself, and it's not taxed at all.” — Warren Buffett

profileTopEducation.schoolName: Gies College of Business - University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

experience.description: I prepared individual tax returns for a top eight public accounting firm in the United States. I worked remotely for their office in Indianapolis, Indiana. I was on their “Center of Excellence” team, which is their department that focuses on helping individuals and families. I was responsible for completing each return in entirety, so then I could pass them off for further review. This job function included communication with clients and superiors to obtain missing information, and create potential  opportunities. While preparing returns, I put in my own time and was expected to exhibit independence and accountability.

As a part of the University of Illinois' revolutionary COVID-19 testing efforts that has kept positivity rates below 1% since it's beginning, I regularly recorded, retrieved, and verified thousands of university affiliates’ personal information using a large database. While doing so I identified and corrected hundreds of discrepancies between current affiliate information and what was in the database. Most notably, I expedited the flow of affiliates entering and inside the testing sites often by speaking articulately and being assertive, resulting in more tests being done and reducing the amount of time spent in line for affiliates, back when no one had been immunized yet.

Tasked with the purpose of coding research in an effort to show course retention, my Interpersonal Communication Professor asked me to be on a team of undergraduate researchers. Our goal was for us to code entries the same way (without prior collaboration) to achieve the highest confidence interval possible. I coded over 800 qualitative data entries using a reference key (a codebook) and feedback. I also collaborated with peers during weekly team meetings, and together, we achieved higher confidence intervals than the graduate students did. The best skill I gained from this experience was the ability to quantify qualitative data methodically using a system that others can follow.

In an effort to find out what it was that made students feel like professors and teaching staff care about them, I was assigned by my boss to conduct informal research. I created a survey using Google Forms, and my professor sent it out to the entire class. The survey had 6 questions. They consisted of: 1 ranking, 1 rating (Likert scale), 1 multiple choice, and 3 short answer questions. After getting the results, I designed a PowerPoint presentation with the responses I collected from 145 students. Then, in one of our meetings, I reported my findings to the teaching team. By analysis through quantification, I was able to convey the survey data in ways that were easy to draw conclusions from, therefore helping my boss to better ensure that her future students feel that their instructors/supervisors care for them.

For two semesters I was a part of a teaching team, thats primary purpose was to help an instructor with an enormous course attendance of over 300 students in person, and over 600 students online. I collaborated with coworkers and superiors during weekly team meetings. In these meetings, we went over responsibilities, shared our ideas, and presented presentations for each other that served as team building exercises. In lecture, we helped to answer questions students had as needed, as well as to help manage their behaviors. I had four tutoring hours each week. In the spring, we were in the Tutoring Center. In the fall, we tutored remotely. There was also a message board online that students could ask questions whenever there wasn't office hours. Over the course of the internship, I aided/guided over 100 students. During the latter half of my internship, I supervised and guided a mentee, that which was assigned to me. In addition to these responsibilities, I developed & revised materials, such as: one-page reviews, learning objectives, informational videos (using Powtoon), and exam questions. I came up with 65 of my own, original exam questions after receiving formal training. The majority of these questions were application-based. Additionally, in January 2020 I took pictures of my boss using a wide variety of angles and locations for her to use in an application to be a keynote speaker at an outside event.

I prepared taxes for a small all-purpose accounting and consulting firm. The firm is owned and operated by three lawyers; two of which who are a part of the #1 ranked accounting faculty in the entire nation, at the Gies College of Business in Champaign, Illinois. At this seasonal position, I catalogued records of over 700 completed returns using an Excel spreadsheet, as well as physical copies of said returns in a file room. I calculated asset allocations, expense categorizations, and created new client IDs and returns for new clients. I also assisted existing and prospective clients in a professional manner in person and on the phone, and contacted several government offices. Ultimately, I prepared over 200 tax returns which included individual and fiduciaries. This experience provided me with the knowledge to understand federal and state tax laws on a basic level, and how they apply to income and expenses.

At Carle Hospital, I was assigned with the task of reviewing and comparing information between Carle's website and their knowledge database. This is because Carle's Human Resources department was looking to no longer use their knowledge database and convert over all of the necessary data to their employee website. In order to help with the transition, I created an Excel spreadsheet which I used to code over 80 necessary and recommended changes. While doing so, I was able to detect over 25 discrepancies between sources as well as advise for over 10 recommendations. It's important to consider that this position was an unpaid internship, thus, I worked mostly less than 10 hours a week.

For two short months, I shadowed a long-time friend of mine who has years of management and entrepreneurial experience. He was the general manager at a brewery in the microbrewery and event hosting industry. By shadowing him, I was able to observe what a day in the life of a manager is like. For example, I helped him conduct up-to-date research within both industries. I brainstormed and collaborated with him and other interns to execute ideas for new promotions. For the operations side of things, I observed and practiced recording inventory. We used price comparison to order inventory. I helped to brand and prepare growlers for wholesale. This was also during a time when the brewery was going through a lot of renovations. Therefore, I completed task-based projects to help with this such as: gardening, decorating, and changing the physical layout of the business. I also helped him host events on weekends, that often featured local musicians or trivia nights. On the marketing side, I assisted with writing creative copy for use in social media posts, and I used social media platforms to do marketing for the business.

This was the pinnacle of my time spent in the service industry. I worked at an upscale restaurant & bar that is attached to a 3-star hotel (the I Hotel) as well as a conference center. For my first six months of work, I waited tables. I made it my goal to understand the ins and the outs of the restaurant, as well as its affiliation with the I Hotel. I worked curiously and diligently, always looking for opportunities to ask questions or better myself. I quickly gained my General Manager’s trust during the first six months I worked there, and as a result I was promoted to Bartender. Shortly after, in January of 2016, I was awarded employee of the month (to read why, see “Honors & awards”). It was through my experience bartending here that I developed strong “real world” people skills. For example, I often managed up to 30 customers per shift while simultaneously assisting up to 8 restaurant servers. While assisting restaurant staff, it was my duty to lead the waitstaff to perform their job function correctly. I learned how to effectively upsell menu items, daily specials, and beverage promotions; as a result, there were times I was able to exceed the daily sales goals by up to 5%. Despite all of this, perhaps what is most memorable of all, has to be all the professional connections I was able to make. As a result of this job, I know a good deal of successful professionals in the Urbana-Champaign, Illinois area.

publications.title: How to reinvent the small-business insurance market for a digital economy
publications.description: Findings from a Deloitte survey of 500 small business owners indicates pandemic may have accelerated shifts in buyer preferences for a wider array of coverage, service, and distribution options. Many small-business respondents are also seeking more diverse and comprehensive solutions, including greater coverage and pricing flexibility, additional risk management services, as well as new sources of insurance.

publications.title: The Rise of the Exponential Underwriter
publications.description: To remain competitive, insurers should accelerate underwriting transformation. They can do this by automating routine tasks and augmenting teams with emerging technology and alternate data sources to empower underwriting professionals to be "exponential" - more valuable than ever. Rather than being displaced by automation, exponential underwriters can multiply their value by gaining new skills and transitioning to a set of enhanced responsibilities. Insurers that continue to rely on traditional ways of underwriting could start a negative spiral that would be difficult to reverse. They may face adverse selection, could drop off preferred lists of distribution partners, and may have a more difficult time recruiting and retaining skilled professionals.

publications.title: Modernizing insurance product development
publications.description: At a time when exceptional client experience is pervasive throughout most other industries, customer-centricity, speed, and flexibility are becoming necessities in insurance product development. As companies such as Amazon and Netflix raise the bar in terms of customer expectations for products and services that are convenient, fast, and personalized, the insurer of the future will likely need to follow suit. And, for all intents and purposes, that future is now.

publications.title: Benefits of a new policy administration system: Why going live is not enough
publications.description: Many P&C insurance carriers embark on core systems transformations, with a focus on policy administration, to enable insurance professionals to more effectively serve customers and provide products for managing personal and business risks. But going live is not enough. What key factors are important for success?

publications.title: The Nimble Insurer: How Technology and Analytics Can Help Insurers Adapt to Changes in the Industry
publications.publishedAt: PCI Marketing and Underwriting Professionals Seminar · Apr 1, 2015
publications.description: Property and casualty carriers recognize the need to become more nimble in order to thrive in an increasingly digital, analytically-driven and efficient marketplace. Companies of all shapes and sizes are making substantial investments to address the challenges that hinder flexibility and agility in delivering high-quality products. This presentation aims to help marketing and underwriting executives understand ways leading companies may reap benefits from investments in modern technology platforms.

publications.publishedAt: 2014 - 2015 Casualty Actuarial Society Ratemaking and Product Management Seminar
publications.description: Leading insurance companies use automated underwriting, powered by analytics, to accelerate profitable growth in the small commercial insurance marketplace.  In fact, industry research indicates that certain small business customers may have an appetite for purchasing commercial insurance direct from carriers.  In response to this emerging trend and financial pressures, automated underwriting initiatives that focus on improving no-touch / low-touch flow rates in existing portfolios, may be part of a disruptive marketplace strategy, or fall somewhere in between.  In these scenarios, achieving business objectives requires consideration of the impacts to product design, pricing, and organizational capabilities.  This presentation covers the challenges and benefits of automated underwriting, illustrated through real life examples and practical experience.

headline: Salesforce Project Manager at Deloitte | Leading Salesforce Implementations
about:
First off, thank you for taking the time to visit my page and welcome! 

Here’s a bit of background about me - When I was 21, I decided to pack my bags and move to the United States after attending school in Mexico, finding myself hungry for new opportunities, and feeling ready for new professional challenges. I would be lying if I said that moving to an entire different culture was easy. My family would be far, my English was rough, and not having my Grandma's cooking within reach would be traumatic. 

Here I am, many years later, an MBA graduate who successfully transitioned from the Higher Ed advising field to a Consultant Manager who is passionate about making everyone around me better. And, yes, my English is far better than in 2005 (thank you Seinfeld episodes with subtitles!)

Over the past 15 years, initially as a Consultant and later as a Manager, I've become involved in leading Project Management efforts for CRM and ERP implementations, managing Consultants in Oracle Cloud implementations (Financials), and Business Organizational Structure efficiency through Enterprise Architecture methodologies. Overall, throughout my career I've become very passionate about coaching individuals and working with teams to achieve professional milestones and overall goals. 

When not saving the world at Deloitte, you'll find me finding new restaurants in Portland, reading a good current events book, playing with my son Sagan and daughter Luna, watching Formula 1, shanking golf balls and wondering what went wrong with my swing, and supporting my Phoenix Suns and Arizona Cardinals. 

If you're interested in learning more about my career and my professional capabilities, I very much welcome a network invite and a coffee if possible! 

Best Regards,
Rafael Quirarte.

publications.title: Defying Dependence: Impacts of H-4 Work Authorization Policy on Immigrant Women, Families, and Communities
publications.publishedAt: South Asian American Policy & Research Institute · Jul 1, 2019
publications.description:
On February 20th, 2019, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) issued a proposal to remove “H-4 dependent spouses from the class of aliens eligible for employment authorization,” which has been under review for months with an uncertain decision date. SAAPRI's latest report, Defying Dependence, incorporates survey data from over 100 South Asian H-4 visa holders, dependent spouses of H-1B workers, and includes in depth profiles of 6 women on the H-4 employment authorization document (EAD) from different parts of the U.S. According to SAAPRI’s findings, rescinding work authorization for H-4 visa holders disproportionately impacts immigrant women and families from South Asian countries. Since the adoption of the H-4 work authorization policy in 2015, 93% of all H-4 EADs were granted to South Asians and 93% were granted to women. 

“Current immigration policy is inequitable for those seeking citizenship and belonging in the U.S from select countries. This report aims to voice the experiences of those directly impacted by pending work authorization policy change in the H-4 community, the vast majority being South Asian women and families,” said Dhara Puvar, Executive Director of SAAPRI. “Our findings reveal that the H-4 EAD rescission is a racial, economic, and gender justice issue.” 

SAAPRI found that revoking the H-4 EAD would have a detrimental impact on economic independence for women, as H-4 visa holders could remain unemployed for up to 10 years or more without the EAD. The report also discusses how the ability to work is closely tied to mental health outcomes for H-4 EAD holders and their families. Defying Dependence calls for the protection of H-4 work authorization and a Congressional solution to the Green Card backlog that will ensure that the H-4 EAD program does not remain a stop-gap solution to current immigration hurdles.

publications.title: Positive Peer Association Among Black American Youth and the Roles of Ethnic Identity and Gender
publications.publishedAt: Journal of Research on Adolescence · Nov 20, 2017
publications.description: This study examined whether peer association, a subtype of peer influence that involves the indirect modeling of behaviors, can promote positive development among Black American adolescents living in high‐risk neighborhoods. Data were collected during a three‐year longitudinal study from a sample of 316 Black American adolescents (M = 11.65 years). As positive peer association increased over time, youth experienced an increase in self‐esteem, school connectedness, paternal and maternal closeness, and a decrease in supportive beliefs about aggression. Additionally, lower ethnic identity appeared to account for why some youth experienced a sharper increase in maternal and paternal closeness as positive peer association increased. Future interventions should consider harnessing the ability of prosocial peers to foster healthy development.

publications.title: The Struggle Overseas: Risk Factors for Suicide among Female Migrant Workers in Nepal
publications.publishedAt: School of International Training (SIT) Digital Collections · Jan 1, 2015
publications.description: This study aims to understand the various risk factors for suicide among female migrant workers in Nepal. Suicide is the leading cause of death among women in the country, and the prevalence of suicide among migrant women in particular warrants further investigation, especially considering the increasing number of women traveling abroad for foreign employment. What experiences do these women have that would lead to suicidal behavior? What personal and institutional challenges contribute to increased risk of suicide? How does the community respond to their needs? This research was conducted in the Kathmandu Valley, with the majority of data acquired through interviews, personal interactions with returnee migrant women, and field observation. This study found that although migration has empowered Nepali women to become financially and socially independent, it is clear that aspects of foreign employment can be detrimental to the mental and emotional well-being of female migrant workers. Risk factors for suicide exist for women over the course of foreign employment – from their departure to their time abroad, and even after their return to Nepal. Although organizations are working towards safer migration, suicide among female migrant workers deserves careful and proactive consideration, as these women are at risk due to societal and institutional factors widely outside of their control.

headline: Deloitte Audit & Assurance Communications Leader
about:
I have built my career around my passion for internal and external corporate communications -- advising senior leaders on communications strategies, developing trust with stakeholders through transparent messaging, and engaging employees during times of transformational change. I serve as the Communications Leader for Deloitte Audit & Assurance, inclusive of CEO and executive communications, workforce communications, change management, employee/talent engagement, and marketing campaigns that align internal audiences with the objectives of the U.S. Audit & Assurance business of Deloitte, the largest of the Big Four professional services firms. In previous lives, I have led stakeholder communications and public/media relations for one of the nation's largest urban school districts, a public housing authority, and two Fortune 500 companies. 

I have lived in some great cities: San Diego, Washington, D.C., and now Chicago. Michigan girl at heart.

I am Accredited in Public Relations (APR) and have served on the board of directors of the Public Relations Society of America as President (San Diego Chapter), Vice President (National Capital Chapter - D.C.), and Board Member (Chicago Chapter).

Expertise:

Strategic Communications: Managed internal and external communications strategies and plans at global companies — ranging from 250 to 100,000+ employees and $4 billion to $18 billion in revenue. Provided C-suite editorial services and communications counsel for CEOs, senior executives, and public/elected officials. 

Public Relations & Media Relations: Served as media spokesperson and PIO for three large organizations. Developed content and pitches to tell organizational story in local, national, and trade media. Advised CEOs and senior leaders, managed strategy, and protected brand during high-profile crises.

Writing & Editing: Served as CEO speechwriter and managing editor of corporate newsletters and magazines. Launched and managed intranets.

experience.description:
Leading team of 25 communications and change management professionals to engage and align audiences with the objectives of Deloitte Audit & Assurance, inclusive of managing CEO and executive communications and eminence, workforce communications, change management, employee/talent engagement, social media, and marketing campaigns. Create, manage, and disseminate content in a highly matrixed, global organization while ensuring message clarity, consistency, and context in relation to the business strategy. Manage online content systems, internal websites, and e-newsletters. Identify and integrate new social media tools into existing communications infrastructure. Monitor metrics for key communications initiatives. 

Deloitte is one of the Big Four professional services firms.

publications.title: Zero Day Threat Detection Using Metric Learning Autoencoders
publications.description: The proliferation of zero-day threats (ZDTs) to companies’ networks has been immensely costly and requires novel methods to scan traffic for malicious behavior at massive scale. The diverse nature of normal behavior along with the huge landscape of attack types makes deep learning methods an attractive option for their ability to capture highly-nonlinear behavior patterns. In this paper, the authors demonstrate an improvement upon a previously introduced methodology, which used a dual-autoencoder approach to identify ZDTs in network flow telemetry. In addition to the previously-introduced asset-level graph features, which help abstractly represent the role of a host in its network, this new model uses metric learning to train the second autoencoder on labeled attack data. This not only produces stronger performance, but it has the added advantage of improving the interpretability of the model by allowing for multiclass classification in the latent space. This can potentially save human threat hunters time when they investigate predicted ZDTs by showing them which known attack classes were nearby in the latent space. The models presented here are also trained and evaluated with two more datasets, and continue to show promising results even when generalizing to new network topologies.

publications.title: Zero Day Threat Detection Using Graph and Flow Based Security Telemetry
publications.description: Zero Day Threats (ZDT) are novel methods used by malicious actors to attack and exploit information technology (IT) networks or infrastructure. In the past few years, the number of these threats has been increasing at an alarming rate and have been costing organizations millions of dollars to remediate. The increasing expansion of network attack surfaces and the exponentially growing number of assets on these networks necessitate the need for a robust AI-based Zero Day Threat detection model that can quickly analyze petabyte-scale data for potentially malicious and novel activity. In this paper, the authors introduce a deep learning based approach to Zero Day Threat detection that can generalize, scale, and effectively identify threats in near real-time. The methodology utilizes network flow telemetry augmented with asset-level graph features, which are passed through a dual-autoencoder structure for anomaly and novelty detection respectively. The models have been trained and tested on four large scale datasets that are representative of real-world organizational networks and they produce strong results with high precision and recall values. The models provide a novel methodology to detect complex threats with low false positive rates that allow security operators to avoid alert fatigue while drastically reducing their mean time to response with near-real-time detection. Furthermore, the authors also provide a novel, labelled, cyber attack dataset generated from adversarial activity that can be used for validation or training of other models. With this paper, the authors’ overarching goal is to provide a novel architecture and training methodology for cyber anomaly detectors that can generalize to multiple IT networks with minimal to no retraining while still maintaining strong performance.

publications.title: Lateral Movement Detection Using User Behavioral Analysis
publications.description: Lateral Movement refers to methods by which threat actors gain initial access to a network and then progressively move through said network collecting key data about assets until they reach the ultimate target of their attack. Lateral Movement intrusions have become more intricate with the increasing complexity and interconnected nature of enterprise networks, and require equally sophisticated detection mechanisms to proactively detect such threats in near real-time at enterprise scale. In this paper, the authors propose a novel, lightweight method for Lateral Movement detection using user behavioral analysis and machine learning. Specifically, this paper introduces a novel methodology for cyber domain-specific feature engineering that identifies Lateral Movement behavior on a per-user basis. Furthermore, the engineered features have also been used to develop two supervised machine learning models for Lateral Movement identification that have demonstrably outperformed models previously seen in literature while maintaining robust performance on datasets with high class imbalance. The models and methodology introduced in this paper have also been designed in collaboration with security operators to be relevant and interpretable in order to maximize impact and minimize time to value as a cyber threat detection toolkit. The underlying goal of the paper is to provide a computationally efficient, domain-specific approach to near real-time Lateral Movement detection that is interpretable and robust to enterprise-scale data volumes and class imbalance.
